sentences.text: The Leonids come from dust left by Comet Tempel-Tuttle, which returns every thirty-three years.
The comet is now near the far end of its orbit; its next perihelion is in 2031.
In mid-November Earth cuts across its orbit almost head-on: the particles enter the atmosphere at seventy-one kilometres a second, the highest speed known.
In an ordinary year fifteen meteors an hour are seen; but in 1833 and 1966 the sky "rained" hundreds of thousands of meteors an hour, and storms came again between 1999 and 2002.
The radiant lies in the head of Leo; with the Moon near new this year, conditions are favourable.
